byteward.title: Moorlark browser blocks third-party trackers by default
byteward.author: Simone Achterberg
body: [f01: The Moorlark browser now blocks third-party trackers by default.] [f02: The change arrives in version 31, which the Moorlark Foundation released on Wednesday.]
Third-party trackers are the scripts that follow people from site to site to build advertising profiles. [f05: In Moorlark's own tests, the browser blocked an average of 23 of them per page.]

[f04: Users can switch blocking off for any site that breaks.] [f03: Moorlark has about 48 million users.] For a browser that size, changing the default is a bigger deal than adding another privacy setting most people never find.

bench-and-bill.title: Moorlark browser blocks third-party trackers by default, drawing a complaint
bench-and-bill.author: Celia Marchetti
body: [f01: Moorlark now blocks third-party trackers by default.] [f03: The browser has about 48 million users.] Advertisers noticed.
[f06: On Wednesday, the Open Ad Markets Coalition filed a complaint with competition regulators, arguing that the change shuts small ad firms out of the market.]

[f07: The change also lands ahead of the Online Tracking Consent Act, which takes effect March 1.] [f08: The law will fine websites up to $5,000 per violation for tracking people without opt-in consent.]
Moorlark's default makes compliance easier for the sites its users visit, which may be the strongest answer to the complaint.

wirefold.title: Moorlark browser now blocks third-party trackers by default
body: The Moorlark browser now blocks third-party trackers by default, starting with version 31, released on Wednesday.
